name: Emily
description: Emily runs a family-operated horticulture farm with her husband and three children. The farm depends heavily on reliable irrigation to maintain crop quality and protect permanent plantings. Changes in water availability can increase operating costs, disrupt production planning and place pressure on the family's main source of income.
goals: Maintain reliable access to water for crop production
Plan planting and production around expected water availability
Keep the family farm financially sustainable as the household's main source of income
concerns: Having to shift toward lower-water-use crops when allocations are uncertain
Securing enough water to protect permanent almond and citrus plantings during low-allocation periods

current.summary: Current water-sharing rules allocate available water according to entitlement type, with General Security users receiving lower and more variable allocations than High Security users.

proposed.summary: Introduce earlier allocation forecasting and targeted irrigation-efficiency support to help farmers plan production and manage periods of low water availability.

name: Jamie Wilson
description: Jamie manages a fictional orchard and vineyard. Permanent plantings need dependable irrigation even when commodity prices soften.

current.summary: Current Victorian water-management rules prioritise entitlement-based allocations and water trading, requiring irrigators to manage seasonal availability and market exposure.

proposed.summary: Expand support for irrigation-efficiency upgrades and longer-term water planning to reduce production risk for farms dependent on permanent plantings.
